title: Cognitive Approach Adventure 2: Schemas & Reconstructive Memory

concepts.def: War of the Ghosts; reconstructive memory
Fitting new info to existing schema

walkthroughs.body_html:
Frederic Bartlett's War of the Ghosts (1932) had British students recall a Native American folk tale.

Recall systematically distorted unfamiliar elements toward Western schemas (canoes → boats; ghosts dropped).

Conclusion: memory is an active reconstruction guided by existing schemas, not a passive replay.

Participants saw a car-crash film, then estimated speed.

The verb in 'how fast were the cars going when they ___?' varied: contacted, hit, smashed.

Mean speeds: contacted 31.8 mph → smashed 40.5 mph. A week later, 'smashed' group falsely recalled broken glass.

Memory is malleable. Eyewitness testimony is reconstructive — subject to leading questions, post-event information and stress.

Practical: cognitive interview techniques, video-recorded statements, and caution before relying on memory in court (Innocence Project DNA exonerations).
